title: 1978 AHSME Problem 20
statement: If \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c\) are nonzero real numbers such that \[ \begin{aligned} \frac{a+b-c}{c} &=\frac{a-b+c}{b}\\ &=\frac{-a+b+c}{a}, \end{aligned} \] and \[ x=\frac{(a+b)(b+c)(c+a)}{abc}, \] and \(x\lt0,\) then \(x\) equals

solutions.text:
Let the common value be \(t.\) The first two resulting equations imply \[ (b-c)(t+2)=0, \] and cyclic comparisons give the analogous relations. Thus either \(a=b=c,\) which gives \(x=8,\) or \(t=-2.\) In the latter case \(a+b=-c,\) \(b+c=-a,\) and \(c+a=-b,\) so \[ x=\frac{(-c)(-a)(-b)}{abc}=-1. \] The condition \(x\lt0\) selects the latter value.

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Set the three equal fractions to \(t\) and compare pairs of the resulting equations
The comparison forces either \(a=b=c\) or \(a+b+c=0\); use the sign of \(x\)
